_source_of_truth: Supersedes the earlier prose shot table, which drifted from what was actually rendered; this file is checked by Scripts/shot_check.py, the prose table never was.
_artifact_why: The ONE path both shot_assemble.py (where it writes) and shot_check.py (where it looks for the assembly stamp beside it) read, so the gate and the assembler cannot drift onto two different files while both report success.
_evidence_files_why: Two shots are footage with a terminal panel composited into the frames, and that panel's text comes from a file on disk that Scripts/terminal_capture.py renders. That module's contract - the terminal panel may only render output a tool actually produced - was enforced by the PROVENANCE OF THE PATH and by nothing else, so it held only for as long as nothing else wrote the path. Something did: an uncommitted driver-equivalence harness exec'd Scripts/pie_bridge_drive.py against a stubbed `unreal`, the driver reached its dump, and its FIXED output path caught the stub's canned returns (IsFalling = 450.000000 - impossible for an FBoolProperty). The gameplay-bridge take's shipped frames were honest; the file backing them was not, for seven hours, with every gate in this repo green. Each entry below records the sha256 of the bytes a shot's frames were rendered from, and shot_check._check_evidence refuses two things: content that is not those bytes, and a file whose mtime is NEWER than the oldest frame in source_dir (a transcript is written during the render and composited afterwards, so it cannot be). The digests are also inside assembly_fingerprint, so changing one makes the MP4 stale by construction. The write side is closed separately and structurally: drivers no longer name a capture path at all - see mt_drive.write_capture_evidence.

shots.title: Cold open - Khaimera + Manny in sync
shots._why_a_rebuild_will_not_reproduce_this: NOT RE-SHOOTABLE, and the one thing missing is the CAMERA. Re-checked against the assets and the surviving capture directory rather than against earlier write-ups. WHAT IS RECOVERABLE: the sequence (Scripts/shot_seq_author.py Seq_Intro, verified field-identical to the shipped asset), the room (Scripts/stage_author.py roster), the three-rig line-up (Manny/Quinn/Khaimera abreast at Y -200 / 0 / +200, with Quinn relocated to Y-3000 off-lane for THIS shot so the pair framing stays tight), the pawn drive (captures/m4-roster/cold_open/_drive.log: add_movement_input +X at Speed 600, gx 0 -> 2912 over 334 ticks, ncams=1) and the fact that Khaimera jogged in place only because his baked pelvis forward-translation was temporarily zeroed for the shoot and re-baked back afterwards. WHAT IS NOT: the camera. Seq_Intro carries a spawnable CineCameraActor with a MovieSceneSpawnTrack and ZERO transform keys (measured, not assumed), so the framing lived only in the driver, and unlike the foot-IK A/B take's harness - which turned out to be sitting in captures/m4-footik-ab/ - this shot's driver .py is on no disk in this project; only its log survives, and the log records the pawns and not the camera. The only surviving description of the framing is 'front-3/4'. The nearest surviving camera geometry is the line-up take's (captures/m4-roster/, its _drive.log: cam = pawnX+912, y 0, z 160, yaw 180, pitch -4), which is a different shot and must not be substituted. Second reason: metahuman_bind.place() has since repositioned the roster pawns onto the current 4-up marks and saved the level, so a rebuild produces the four-rig stage, not the three-rig one.

shots._evidence_correction: (The file 'hashed above' in this paragraph is the take that replaced the corrupted transcript, 5f9fbee7...; the row now hashes the take re-shot against the aim-offset fix, see _note_reshoot.) THIS ROW USED TO END by claiming that the terminal-panel transcript re-captured in that render was byte-identical to the one it replaced. That claim was false against the file on disk and is retracted, not edited away. A later check found captures/m9-bridge/bridge_output.txt containing IsFalling = 450.000000 and GroundedFlag = 450.000000 - readings AnimDebugTools::GetAnimVariable cannot produce for an FBoolProperty - written seven hours after the frames it backed, by an uncommitted equivalence harness driving the driver against a stubbed `unreal`. The shipped MP4 was never affected; the frame at t=38.5s pulled out of the encoded artifact shows the correct transcript. The fix taken here is the self-consistent one rather than the cheap one: the gameplay-bridge take's 240 frames were RE-RENDERED from a real MRQ run (M9_Shot2b_Bridge, success=True, luma [129.47, 130.19, 131.23] against the superseded take's [129.48, 130.19, 131.24]) and re-composited from that run's own transcript, which is the file hashed above. Nothing was reconstructed from pixels. The byte-identical claim is NOT restored for the new take, because the new take's GetAnimDebugState dump is this graph's current one and the superseded file is gone - a claim of byte-identity is exactly the kind of unverifiable assertion this correction exists to remove.
shots._caption_correction: THE CAPTION USED TO READ 'Three variables are the whole animator-to-engineer interface.' Retired because the graph contradicts it: Plugins/MotionTerminal/Tests/Baselines/abp_mt_locomotion.json binds AimYaw and AimPitch to node 7's X/Y and WeaponIKAlpha to node 12's Alpha, and Scripts/army_conductor.py:55 calls TurnYawDelta/AimYaw/AimPitch/WeaponIKAlpha 'pure inputs' in those words. It was true of the first locomotion graph and went stale when the aim offset and hand IK were added. It also defeated shot_check._check_caption_binding, whose NUM_RE only matches digits, so a SPELLED-OUT numeral is an uncited numeric assertion the gate cannot see - noted in that function's docstring. The replacement asserts only what the terminal panel demonstrates: one write to CharacterMovementComponent.Velocity, and Speed/IsFalling/GroundedFlag following it. Captions are burned in, so this cost a re-assemble, which the re-render above required anyway.

shots.title: Crowd pull-back + budget
shots._note_reshoot: RE-SHOT against the aim-offset fix (army_spawn spawn, Scripts/shot_render.py 06, despawn). The spawn reported hero 6 / mid 8 / far 32 with 0 meshless; the render's per-second ARMYPULL lines read army=46 dressed=46 from t=1.03 to t=8.03, with cond=True on each (the t=0.02 line precedes the conductor's bootstrap at tick 3). shot_render now FAILS a 06 take without army=46: its first two attempts passed capture_check with an EMPTY stage (army=0), because the tool reloaded the level and dropped the unsaved crowd, and those runs' log lines are also in this take's _shoot_log.json (the log search spanned the editor session; shot_render now keeps only lines logged after its own render starts). The allocator stays OFF in this take, which is the condition the caption's 3.6 / 4.0 ms was measured under. That measurement predates moving the crowd's two Khaimeras onto the in-place graph; re-measuring with the allocator on is still open: both in-editor routes to the stats read crashed the editor.
shots._fps_in_correction: Was 30 in an earlier revision. Seq_Army has a 60/1 display rate (Scripts/shot_seq_author.py), so these 480 frames are 8 s of sequence time consumed 1:1 into a 30 fps timeline - i.e. this shot plays at HALF SPEED, like the foot-IK A/B and turn/aim/hand-IK takes, and the manifest asserted real-time. fps_in is documentation only (shot_assemble passes fps_out to ffmpeg and nothing reads fps_in), so correcting it changes no pixels and no duration; it stops the field lying about what the viewer sees.
shots.caption_text: 46 instances: game-thread 3.6 / 4.0 ms, inside the budget that is asserted every run.

shots._why_the_driver_is_new: The harness that first shot this take (army_take_driver.py + mrq_render.py) was scratchpad-only and never committed, so neither the camera path nor the invocation existed anywhere in the repo - the same repeatability gap Seq_Lane had, and worse. Scripts/pie_army_pullback_drive.py is that harness's pullback branch, promoted and committed, and the geometry is unchanged: same 8.0 s smoothstep from (760,150,175) to (7200,0,2900), same 20 mm, same 480 frames off Seq_Army at 60 fps. The camera's read-back position and focal length are now logged every second by the shipped render itself, so the framing is witnessed rather than asserted.
shots._the_measured_figures_were_not_re-derive: Neither cited number comes from this render and neither was recomputed. 46 is hero 6 + mid 8 + far 32 out of army_config.json (re-checked against that file every pytest run by test_crowd_instance_count_matches_army_config_rings); 3.6 / 4.0 ms is army_config budget._measured / gt_ms_ceiling from the driven crowd sweep. What the re-render adds is a WITNESS: the shipped render's own log reads `army=46` on every one of its per-second lines, and the spawn that fed it reported hero 6 / mid 8 / far 32 with 0 meshless.
